title: A common finite etale cover detecting irreducibility of a finite family
statement:
Let $X$ be a connected Noetherian separated scheme, let $\bar x$ be a geometric point of $X$, and let $\ell$ be a prime invertible on $X$. Put $\Pi=\pi_1(X,\bar x)$ [def-galois-fibre-functor] and $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $\mathcal F_1,\ldots,\mathcal F_r$ be irreducible lisse $\Qlb$-sheaves [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], where irreducible means nonzero with no proper nonzero lisse subsheaf; allow $r=0$.

There exist, for each $j$, a finite extension $E_j/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Qlb$, a finite-dimensional continuous representation $\rho_j:\Pi\to\operatorname{GL}_{E_j}(V_j)$ [def-pod-l-adic-representations], and a $\Pi$-equivariant isomorphism $V_j\otimes_{E_j}\Qlb\cong(\mathcal F_j)_{\bar x}$ for the natural stalk action. There are $\rho_j$-stable full lattices $L_j\subset V_j$ (finite free $\mathcal O_{E_j}$-submodules spanning $V_j$), uniformizers $\varpi_j$ and integers $N_j\geq1$, a finite group $Q$ and a continuous surjective homomorphism $q:\Pi\twoheadrightarrow Q$ such that
$$\ker q=\bigcap_{j=1}^r\ker\bigl(\Pi\longrightarrow\operatorname{GL}(L_j/\varpi_j^{N_j}L_j)\bigr).$$
There is a connected finite etale cover $p:T\to X$ [def-galois-categories] and a $\Pi$-equivariant bijection $|T_{\bar x}|\cong Q$, where $\Pi$ acts on $Q$ by $g\cdot a=q(g)a$. For every subgroup $H\subseteq\Pi$ satisfying $q(H)=Q$, each $V_j\otimes_{E_j}\Qlb$, with the action restricted to $H$, is irreducible (nonzero with no proper nonzero invariant subspace).

source.place: proof, first six sentences: finite-stage representations, finite matrix witnesses, intersection of kernels and connected finite etale Galois cover; detection conclusion from the sentence on surjecting onto each reduction quotient

proof.text: For each $j$, write $\mathcal F_j$ as a lisse $E_j$-sheaf extended to $\Qlb$, with $E_j/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, using the pair description in [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves](4). Apply [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2) over $E_j$. Its fibre functor gives a finite-dimensional continuous $E_j$-representation $V_j$, and its scalar-extension compatibility identifies $V_j\otimes_{E_j}\Qlb$ equivariantly with $(\mathcal F_j)_{\bar x}$ for the natural stalk action. The connected, Noetherian, separated and $\ell$-invertible hypotheses required by that corollary are exactly the hypotheses on $X$.

source.place: proof: finite coefficient fields, finite reduction quotients, and intersection of open normal kernels

proof.text: The exact $\Qlb$-equivalence of [cor-galois-lisse-representations](2) makes these stalk representations irreducible. Here every invariant vector subspace is an object of the representation category in [def-pod-l-adic-representations](3): choose a basis of an invariant subspace $W\subset V_j\otimes\Qlb$ in reduced column-echelon form and a finite extension $L/E_j$ containing its finitely many coordinates. If $W_L$ is its $L$-span, pivot coordinates give $W\cap(V_j\otimes L)=W_L$. Every group element has its matrix in $E_j$, so it preserves this intersection; the pivot coordinates also express its action on $W_L$ as linear combinations over $L$ of the original continuous matrix entries. Thus $W_L$ is a continuous finite-dimensional $L$-representation and $W=W_L\otimes_L\Qlb$. A nonzero proper $W$ would therefore give a nonzero proper subobject under the exact equivalence, contradicting the assumed irreducibility of $\mathcal F_j$. Nonzeroness is reflected by an equivalence as well.

source.place: proof: finite coefficient fields, finite reduction quotients, and intersection of open normal kernels

proof.text: On a small skeleton of the finite locally constant category, the fibre functor of [def-galois-fibre-functor] has finite values and its automorphism group has the evaluation topology. Apply [lem-galois-aut-profinite] to conclude that $\Pi$ is profinite, in particular a compact topological group.

By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $\mathcal O_{E_j}$ is a DVR with fraction field $E_j$, finite residue field, and uniformizer $\varpi_j$. Apply [lem-pod-profinite-stable-lattice] to the jointly continuous action from step 1 and compact group from step 3 to choose a stable full finite free lattice $L_j$. Apply the recorded statement of [lem-zl-finite-matrix-irreducibility] using step 2: it gives a possibly different stable lattice $D_j$ and $m_j\geq1$ detecting irreducibility modulo $\varpi_j^{m_j}D_j$. To use precisely that statement, compare the lattices explicitly. Express finite generators of $D_j$ in a basis of $L_j$, and express the finitely many basis vectors of $L_j$ in the $E_j$-span of generators of $D_j$. The finitely many coefficients lie in $E_j$; their valuations are bounded below. Choose $a_j\geq0$ making all coefficients integral after multiplication by $\varpi_j^{a_j}$. Then $\varpi_j^{a_j}L_j\subseteq D_j\subseteq\varpi_j^{-a_j}L_j$. Set $N_j=m_j+2a_j\geq1$. If $\rho_j(h)-\rho_j(g)$ maps $L_j$ into $\varpi_j^{N_j}L_j$, then it maps $D_j$ into $\varpi_j^{N_j-a_j}L_j\subseteq\varpi_j^{m_j}D_j$. Hence any subgroup with the same reduction image on $L_j/\varpi_j^{N_j}L_j$ also has the same image on $D_j/\varpi_j^{m_j}D_j$ and acts absolutely irreducibly. This also agrees with the current given-integral-basis matrix-witness formulation, which applies directly to a basis of $L_j$.

source.place: proof: finite coefficient fields, finite reduction quotients, and intersection of open normal kernels

proof.text: Put $A_j=\mathcal O_{E_j}/\varpi_j^{N_j}\mathcal O_{E_j}$ and $M_j=L_j/\varpi_j^{N_j}L_j$. By [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], $A_j$ is finite and $\varpi_j^{N_j}\mathcal O_{E_j}=\mathfrak m_{E_j}^{N_j}$. A lattice basis identifies $M_j$ with a finite power of $A_j$, so $\operatorname{Aut}_{A_j}(M_j)$ is finite. Stability gives a homomorphism $\alpha_j:\Pi\to\operatorname{Aut}_{A_j}(M_j)$. For continuity, use the jointly continuous action in [def-pod-l-adic-representations](2), furnished in step 1. In a lattice basis, the topology of $V_j$ is the product topology on $E_j^{d_j}$, and $L_j$ corresponds to $\mathcal O_{E_j}^{d_j}$. Since $\mathfrak m_{E_j}^{N_j}=\varpi_j^{N_j}\mathcal O_{E_j}$ is an open ball about zero, every coset of $\mathfrak m_{E_j}^{N_j}L_j$ is open in $L_j$ for its subspace topology. Evaluation of the action on each basis vector followed by reduction is therefore continuous to the finite discrete module $M_j$. A linear automorphism of $M_j$ is determined by those basis images, so the finite tuple of evaluations embeds its automorphism group into a finite discrete product. This proves continuity of $\alpha_j$, and hence $K_j=\ker\alpha_j$ is open and normal.

source.place: proof: finite coefficient fields, finite reduction quotients, and intersection of open normal kernels

proof.text: Define $\alpha=(\alpha_j)_j$ with target the finite product of the preceding finite automorphism groups, let $Q=\alpha(\Pi)$ with its discrete topology, and let $q:\Pi\to Q$ be $\alpha$ with codomain restricted to its image. This is a continuous surjective homomorphism to a finite group, and $q(g)=1$ if and only if every $\alpha_j(g)=1$. Thus $K=\ker q=\bigcap_jK_j$ is the required open normal subgroup. If $r=0$, the product and $Q$ are the trivial group and this intersection is $\Pi$.

source.place: proof: finite coefficient fields, finite reduction quotients, and intersection of open normal kernels

proof.text: Apply the pointed form of [cor-galois-open-subgroups] to the open subgroup $K$. It supplies a nonempty connected finite etale cover $p:T\to X$ and $t\in|T_{\bar x}|$ with stabilizer exactly $K$. The category of finite etale covers is a Galois category by [lem-fet-galois-category]; since $T$ is connected as a scheme, [lem-galois-finite-etale-connected-object] makes it a connected object. Then [lem-galois-transitive] says that $\Pi$ acts transitively on its fibre. Define $Q\to|T_{\bar x}|$ by $q(g)\mapsto g\cdot t$. If $q(g)=q(h)$, then $h^{-1}g\in K$, so $g\cdot t=h\cdot t$; the same implication reversed proves injectivity, and transitivity proves surjectivity. The identity $(ag)\cdot t=a\cdot(g\cdot t)$ proves equivariance for the regular left action on $Q$. Invert this bijection for the stated fibre identification. For $r=0$ one can take $T=X$ and the identity cover.

source.place: proof: finite coefficient fields, finite reduction quotients, and intersection of open normal kernels

proof.text: Finally let $H\subseteq\Pi$ satisfy $q(H)=Q$. For each $g\in\Pi$, choose $h\in H$ with $q(h)=q(g)$. Then $h^{-1}g\in\ker q\subseteq\ker\alpha_j$ for every $j$, so $\alpha_j(h)=\alpha_j(g)$. Hence $H$ and $\Pi$ have exactly the same reduction image on each $M_j$. The conclusion of [lem-zl-finite-matrix-irreducibility] for the lattices and integers of step 4 gives irreducibility of every $V_j\otimes_{E_j}\Qlb$ under $H$. No closedness of $H$ is used: only equality of these finite images is needed. For the empty family this conclusion is vacuous.
